analysis:
Only docs/operations/provider-release.md changed (base lines 174, 497-532; head 174-176, 499-541). It is documentation of the release pipeline, with no executable code. The visible patch excerpt is truncated: it is cut off mid-way through the Dev-Branch Lane rewrite. It shows step 3 moving from a push-triggered release-preparation cache to a daily SDK 27 release-preparation schedule (`47 6 * * *`, gated on provider-swift/libs changes). It also shows the dev-branch lane moving from push-triggered to a 6-hour schedule (`23 */6 * * *`) plus manual workflow_dispatch on refs/heads/dev. The excerpt says the scheduled `gate` job runs on free ubuntu without secrets.

I examined the base text for the controls these edits describe: the source gate (verify_workflow_source requiring a GitHub-verified commit on dev ancestry), secret scoping (the PROD_*/STAGING_* secrets are guarded by environment checks), the signing-key lifetime, and the Developer ID requirement. Nothing in the visible patch removes or weakens these controls. The docs are consistent with the retained T-054, TB-011 and A-011 posture.

I could not verify the head text of the new dev-branch lane, including whether the scheduled and dispatch paths keep the source gate and dev-only secret scoping. The docs describe a gate job without secrets, which is consistent with those controls. I also could not verify that release-dev-branch.yml, which is outside the supplied evidence, actually implements what the docs describe. That workflow should be checked for: (a) dispatch restricted to refs/heads/dev; (b) the schedule/dispatch ref being the dev branch SHA the gate resolved; (c) secrets: inherit still reaching only DEV_* for the dev environment. No concrete security regression is evidenced, but the truncated excerpt leaves part of the change unseen.

The cache details in T-041 are not affected.
